kicker: Scenario's kinetic-film skill, read and measured

scenes.headline: How a launch film becomes one web page
scenes.sub: Scenario's kinetic-film skill, read file by file
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Tempo! A Claude skill turns a short brief into a launch film. Here is how, and what its quality gate can see.

scenes.text: A film is a spec of scene blocks on the beats of its music. Every frame is a pure function of time.
scenes.say: The film is a list of scene blocks on the beats of the music. Every frame depends only on the time, so a renderer can jump anywhere.

steps.say: The agent turns the brief into a spec of scene blocks, each placed between two beats.
Scenario's tools make what code cannot draw: the music at an exact tempo and the sound effects.
The engine draws the spec as a web page, and headless Chrome grabs several sub-frames for each output frame.
Python averages the samples for motion blur, adds bloom and grain, and x264 writes the film.

scenes.title: How the gate judges motion
scenes.say: Before handing a film over, the skill measures it three ways.

items.say: At most forty percent of frames may be still.
No hold over point six seconds before the end card.
Median motion of at least two and a half pixels a frame.

scenes.label: speed a big box needs to count as moving
scenes.say: A frame counts as moving when one and a half percent of it changes. A big box needs about forty-three pixels a frame to do that.

scenes.text: Cut on the beat is not the same as never park. The gate sees big moves and is blind to slow drift.
scenes.say: Cutting on the beat is not the same as never parking. The gate sees big moves, and is blind to slow drift.

recap: Spec in beats, frames from time
Music and sounds from Scenario MCP
A gate that sees only big motion
scenes.say: To recap: a spec in beats, frames from time, sound from Scenario, and a gate that only sees big motion.
